clock.passport.title: Passport
clock.passport.expired: Expired. Renew it before you travel or file anything new.
clock.passport.soon: Under 6 months left. Many trips and filings need more, so renew early.
clock.passport.ok: Keep at least 6 months on it before any trip.
clock.i94.title: Authorized stay (I-94)
clock.i94.passed: This date has passed. Talk to an immigration attorney today.
clock.i94.visitor: Overstaying even a day can cancel your visa. To stay longer, file Form I-539 before this date.
clock.i94.work: This, not your visa stamp, is when your stay ends. Extensions can usually be filed up to 6 months ahead.
clock.i94.other: This, not your visa stamp, is when your stay ends. Any extension has to be filed before it.
clock.visa.title: Visa stamp
clock.visa.expired: Expired, which is fine while you stay inside the US. You need a new one before you re-enter.
clock.visa.ok: Only matters when you re-enter the US. It doesn’t decide how long you can stay.
clock.ead.expired.title: Work permit (EAD)
clock.ead.expired: Expired. You may not be allowed to work until the renewal is approved, so check with your attorney or HR.
clock.ead.window.title: EAD renewal window
clock.ead.window: Opens 180 days before your card expires. Most renewals filed since {date} get no automatic extension, so file on day one.
clock.ead.renew.title: Renew your work permit
clock.ead.renew: The renewal window is open. File Form I-765 now: it has to be approved before this date for you to keep working.
clock.unemployment.title: {program} unemployment days
clock.unemployment.usedUp: You’ve used every unemployment day. Talk to your DSO today.
clock.unemployment.running: Running. Every day without qualifying work counts, weekends and days abroad too. {left} left.
clock.unemployment.paused: Paused while you work. {left} of {limit} left. Report new jobs within 10 days.
clock.unemployment.pausedStem: Paused while you work. {left} of {limit} left across OPT and STEM OPT. Report new jobs within 10 days.
clock.grace.title: {days}-day grace period
clock.optEnd.title: {program} ends
clock.optEnd.after: Your OPT has ended. Before this date: change status, start a new program, or leave.
clock.optEnd.before: After this you get {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} to change status, start a new program, or leave.
clock.stem.title: STEM OPT extension window
clock.stem.open: Open now if your degree is on the STEM list. USCIS has to receive it before your OPT ends.
clock.stem.later: If your degree is on the STEM list, you can apply for 24 more months from this date.
clock.optWindow.title: OPT application window
clock.optWindow.open: Open. USCIS must receive your I-765 within 30 days of your DSO’s recommendation, while your stay is still valid.
clock.optWindow.later: Opens 90 days before your program ends and closes {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after.
clock.f1.grace: After your program ends you have {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} to start OPT, transfer, change status, or leave.
clock.dsCap.title: Extension of stay needed
clock.dsCap: D/S now ends on {date} at the latest. Your program runs longer, so file Form I-539 before then. Any trip abroad gets you a fixed I-94 date instead.
clock.j1.grace: J-1 programs come with 30 days after the end date to prepare and leave. Extensions go through your sponsor.
clock.grace.jobEnds: Your job ends {date}. From the next day you get up to 60 days, or until your I-94 date if that comes first.
clock.grace.running: Before this date: a new employer files for you, you change status, or you leave. An attorney can help you pick fast.
clock.h1bMax.title: H-1B six-year limit
clock.h1bMax: Six years from {date}, plus {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} abroad you can win back. A green card in process can extend it.
clock.ap.title: Travel needs advance parole
clock.ap: Leaving while your I-485 is pending can abandon it, unless you have advance parole or keep valid H or L status.
clock.i90.open.title: Renew your green card
clock.i90.later.title: Green card renewal opens
clock.i90.expired: Your card has expired. Your status hasn’t, but you need a valid card to travel and work. File Form I-90.
clock.i90.ok: Your status doesn’t expire, only the card does. You can renew with Form I-90 in the last 6 months.
clock.i751.open.title: Remove conditions now
clock.i751.later.title: Remove-conditions window
clock.i751.expired: Your conditional card has expired. Talk to an immigration attorney now.
clock.i751.ok: File Form I-751 (I-829 for EB-5) in the 90 days before your 2-year card expires.
clock.n400.now.title: You can apply for citizenship
clock.n400.later.title: Citizenship window
clock.n400.now: You can file Form N-400 now, as long as your time abroad fits the rules below.
clock.n400.later: You can file Form N-400 from this date: 90 days before your {years}-year green card anniversary.
clock.presence.title: Travel budget for citizenship
clock.presence.over: You’ve spent {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} too many abroad for this window. Your filing date may need to move.
clock.presence.ok: About {days, plural, one {# more day} other {# more days}} abroad before {date} still keeps you over the {required}-day presence rule.
clock.residence.broken.title: Continuous residence broken
clock.residence.long.title: Long trip: continuous residence
clock.residence.broken: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} away. A year or more breaks continuous residence, so the clock restarts.
clock.residence.atRisk: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} away. Trips of 6 months or more can break continuous residence. Keep proof of your US ties.
clock.residence.watch: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} away. At 180 days this trip starts to count against continuous residence.
clock.queue.title: Green card queue
clock.queue: Priority date {date}{extra}. Waiting {wait}. Compare it with this month’s Visa Bulletin.
time.inDays: in {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
time.daysAgo: {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago
ask.i94.hint: On your I-94 record at i94.cbp.dhs.gov
